$comment: P68 round 9 (lane `cs`; routed by the coordinator from lane mig's `int x = 1 + "never";`): an ARRAY operand of `+` / `-` decays to a pointer to its first element (C 6.3.2.1p3) on either side of `+`, so `a + 1`, `1 + a` and `a - 0` are `int *` and `1 + "never"` is `char *` — in `sizeof`, in `_Generic`, as a pointer initializer or argument, and as the POINTER an int initializer converts (the row-1 class: S_IntegerPointerConversion at 22:13). ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23, each reference separately and this file compiled and RUN: gcc 13.3.0 and mingw-w64 13.2.0 at -std=c2x and MSVC 19.51 at /std:c17 and /std:clatest (C4047) build it with that one warning and exit 42; clang 18.1.3 refuses the int initializer (-Wint-conversion is an error there) and -std=c17 -pedantic-errors refuses it on gcc and mingw. Before this round (✔MEASURED, the lane's fold-3 build) DSS typed `1 + a` as the INTEGER and `a + 1` as the ARRAY: `sizeof(a + 1)` was 40 and `sizeof(1 + a)` 4 (every reference: 8), `_Generic(1 + a, int *: …)` missed, `int x = 1 + "never";` drew no diagnostic and `char const *s = 1 + "never";` a wrong integer-to-pointer one — the lowering was already right, so the program ran; only the semantic type was wrong. exit 42 = every size, type and value is C's.
